A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Optimal Token Baseline study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-F are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning experiments, benchmark scores in Table 1, training curves, and ablations in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, training analyses, and ablations, including the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The cumulative-energy baseline, Logit-Gradient Proxy, empirical estimator, and off-policy extension are unchanged. Revised explanations do not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both use DAPO-MATH-17k for training and MATH500, AMC23, AIME24, and AIME25 for evaluation. Single-turn reasoning, tool-integrated reasoning, and the longer-response and additional-turn scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 1 retains GRPO, RLOO, OPO, OGB, and SimpleTIR in their corresponding settings. The GRPO-with-TIS/MIS comparisons and baseline variants are also retained.

E3.justification: The model configurations, on-policy training protocol, budgets, decoding settings, and avg@32 evaluation remain unchanged. Table 3 consolidates existing settings and newly names the optimizer; it does not establish a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Both contain the group-size ablation, length-versus-logit proxy comparisons, longer-context tests, training-stability diagnostics, and isolated-energy comparison. Repositioned appendix plots contain no new analyses.

E5.justification: No seed information, independent-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised. The existing evaluation averaging and Appendix E variance-estimation procedure are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 values and the plotted results are unchanged, including OTB's AIME25 scores of 30.31 for single-turn reasoning and 28.13 for TIR. The reported token reductions remain 66.03% and 68.32%; new Table 3 contains settings rather than results.

T1.justification: The equations, theorems, proofs, and Appendix A-E derivations are unchanged. Section 4 now explicitly mentions structural conditions and the intractable objective, but Appendix C already contained those assumptions and approximations in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about token-level variance reduction, the forward-pass proxy, training stability, and sample efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of training collapse, gradient heterogeneity, proxy limitations, and applicability remain unchanged. The added qualification before Theorem 4.1 foregrounds limitations already documented in Appendix C rather than introducing a new boundary.

D1.justification: New Table 3 in Appendix F.1 identifies AdamW as the optimizer, previously unspecified, and collects the training hyperparameters in one place. Most entries repeat existing disclosures; implementation-framework and access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The Dayan and Gur-Ari reference edits update bibliographic details without adding or replacing cited research.

P1.justification: The introduction and portions of Sections 4.1 and 5.1 receive limited wording revisions. v2 also adds acknowledgements and updates affiliations and publication text while preserving the scientific section order.

P2.justification: v2 adds the hyperparameter table and makes modest figure-sizing and placement changes. Appendix plots are regrouped across pages, while their graphics, axes, legends, and results remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The AdamW disclosure and consolidated Table 3 modestly improve reproducibility and accessibility of the settings. Section 4 also makes the pre-existing theoretical qualifications more visible. These are useful documentation improvements, while the scientific evidence and derivations remain unchanged.
